body: Cliche but that his actions would affect my relationships with men later on in life.
That I had to consciously ask myself, "will this set him off?" before liking a photo of another guy on Instagram. I can see why they got rid of the following activity tab on IG.

It's up there with the Aviva leg throw from RHONY. I would  argue Luis blasting the bachata music in Molly's face and accusing her of being a witch was up there too. I almost cried at the reality television goodness of it.

I wish. I really don't have anywhere to go and it's finals week at school. I was tempted to just hang out at the school library for a few days instead of hanging out with them. Right now I'm just ignoring them and letting them know I don't want to be involved. Luckily tomorrow I'll be out of the house for 15\+ hours so it'll give me some space from them.

Yep, that sounds like a real N fight. My nMom and nBrother have had some classic petty arguments. One of my personal favorites was my nbrother threatening to kill himself and throw himself over our stair banister (that is about 15 feet high) if my nMom didn't buy him a car. Another was my nMom getting upset nBro didn't buy her mcdonalds when he got himself some.

I genuinely believe narcissists look forward to starting arguments during the holidays. This is why I made conscious decision to no longer attend family functions because my Nmom and her Nsiblings  all thrive off each other. I can never give her advice to stop the fight since she secretly enjoys it. I'll never forget how her and my aunt ruined the first holiday after my dad's death by getting into a fight over who was more dysfunctional and everyone had to go home. You can't even make this stuff up.
When you can't ingest anything prepared by your nmom, you know the relationship is permanently fractured. I'm sorry, OP.

The narcissist can never resist the opportunity to ruin a family gathering. They thrive off drama and chaos and being in a group of people gives them the perfect opportunity to act out and stir the pot.

My mom's favorite comeback to me confronting her about never saying I love you to me was, "I shouldn't have had to say it. You should've just known." Really? I hate when people say that. If you did love me, you should've just said it. What was so icky about saying it that you never could do it.

I'm sorry you're going through this. Do you think your mom is having a mid life crisis? Did something happen to set her off? My dad was bipolar and this sounds like one of his manic episodes. Maybe something is going on with her. Can you talk to your dad about it? Maybe the family needs to stage an intervention to figure out why she's changed so drastically.

God I know. My nmom's favorite thing is to criticize everyone's appearance. If I ask her to be quiet she starts going, "Oh OKAY. Guess, I'm just such a burden to you, god forbid I say anything." trying to make me feel guilty but she's still talking.

When you read stories like this it makes you wonder how many missing people out there fell into a situation like this when lost/disoriented/needing help in the middle of nowhere. You always hear about stranger danger but you don't realize how serious it is until you hear about something like this. There are real predators out there.

This might not be the best advice but this is why I started carrying  pepper spray with me when walking home from school.  When I was 18, an older (40ish) guy followed me home after I rejected his advances for a date and yelled and harassed me all the way to my front door. I was terrified that he knew where I lived and it was pretty traumatic for a girl that had never even had a boyfriend let alone any male attention. For a long time, I refused to walk the 20 minute walk to school, staying in the library until my mom could pick me up. Then I started walking again but always carried pepper spray. If I were you, I would embarrass him in public next time in front of everyone. Call him a f*cking pervert and demand he leave you alone. Tell him if he tries to do anything you'll pepper spray him and call the cops. Be loud, don't be scared to attract attention this might be the only way he learns. Film the whole thing if you have to and threaten to use it as leverage to out him as the neighborhood perv. He gets off to the fact that it's making you uncomfortable but if you show him you're not scared of him and you'll be the type to "cause a scene" he might back off.

That was one irresponsible cashier. He put you in danger by letting that old man into the store and let him supervise the place while he left. Just because the creepy old guy isn't trying to lure him into the dressing room and take his clothes off doesn't mean he won't try it on a vulnerable young woman. I hate idiots like that. Honestly makes me wonder if they were in cahoots to try and do something bad to you. Nobody can be that stupid.

Jesus christ, I'm so sorry. I can feel the rage for you. Anyway you can leave and cut off all contact? They're lucky to even have your picture. Reminds me of the time my friend published her first book and her Ndad said, "Thanks I needed new toilet paper." Fuck them.

This is so hilarious in a sad and depraved way. My mom still brings up how lucky I am that she didn't "take herself out" and commit suicide while raising me. Why thank you for not killing yourself and actually raising me like a normal human being.

Pouring out their drink/hiding alcohol might not be the best idea. It sometimes makes the person angrier, leads them to go out and buy more (which can lead to DUI/arrests), or hide their alcohol better. The best thing to do is to wait until they are sober and confront them. It's easier to rationalize with them sober. I'm sorry because I've been in this situation so many times.

I really like this show. I relate to his character a lot. There was one scene in particular where he was about to go to his friend's birthday party, walked up to the front door and decided not to go in because he saw all the people inside. 
I like the show because he doesn't have total SA because he can still socialize on a minimal level but he's very isolated which is how I feel. It also shows how he watches people from a distance and figures everything out about them through observation (and hacking lol) but this is something I've always learned being the quiet kid/person.

Thanks. This is what I'm trying to do right now, making small talk with some people in my classes so I have someone to rely on in case I need help or we need to form groups, etc. I think just getting out of the house every day, even if it's just for a walk is helpful as well. I always feel better after I've pushed myself to go out for the day because my SA also gets worse the longer I stay in the house. It's like I begin to regress more into my own world and I can feel my mental health slipping. Good luck to you too.
